<reason>Both sides were competent and the clash was well-focused, but CON did more damaging comparative work. PRO's strongest asset was the line it drew in [A2.2] (price varies with product/transaction vs. inferred personal profile) plus a genuinely good closing reframe: personalized pricing exists precisely to identify who will not open the "second tab," so market discipline cannot substitute for disclosure. CON, however, turned PRO's own line against it twice ([B2.3], [B4.7]): PRO's flagship villain — the desperate midnight shopper facing few sellers — is priced on time and local competition, i.e. transaction features, hence permitted under PRO's rule, while retention/churn-risk and targeted-coupon discounts are pure profile and thus captured. PRO never squarely answered that inversion despite it being flagged in two consecutive speeches and again in closing; that left CON's "scalpel held backwards" framing standing. CON also built a clean dilemma on disclosure: PRO's A4.1 concession that disclosure need not publish individual amounts shrinks it to a cookie banner with no bite, while a version with bite triggers the discount-withdrawal dynamic PRO never rebutted directly (PRO's student/senior counterexamples are legible categories with a public moral story, a distinction CON drew persuasively). PRO's answers to pressure questions were properly labelled and partly responsive, but CON's answers were both labelled and more directly load-bearing (the marginal-shopper mechanism explained without needing the firm to know who the shopper is). Finally, CON offered explicit weighing — who bears the cost of error, the firm under a narrow ban versus the marginal buyer who simply gets no ticket — while PRO's weighing stayed largely at the level of trust and consent. PRO also carried a small execution cost from a clipped opening. Clear but competitive win for CON.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B2.3]-[B2.4] inversion: PRO's product-versus-profile line bans the churn-risk discount while licensing the surcharge on the desperate late-night buyer (time and local competition being transaction features). Restated in [B4.7] and closing, it went unanswered by PRO and undercut PRO's claim to a workable, targeted rule.</best_rebuttal>
